summary: A one-knob config change (BLOCK_N 64->128 on the sliding decode path, S=16) whose per-shape _sliding_fused_kernel rows read cleanly without a companion; the mechanism is plausible, but the gain is modest and may be partly pre-empted by num_stages=2 pipelining already overlapping the second tile's gather.
justification: Arithmetic checks out against master: kernel_fn routes every sliding q_len==1 shape to _sliding_forward with splits=16 and BLOCK_N=64; count = 2047 at an 80K context, so chunk = ceil(2047/16)=128 (already a multiple of 64), i.e. exactly two loop iterations per program, and BLOCK_N=128 gives one iteration (the last split gets 127 keys, masked). The profile backs a latency-bound picture: sliding decode_1 is 10.4 us for about 0.5 MB (floor 0.1 us), decode_16 is 12.9 us (floor 1.6), decode_32 is 22.1 us (floor 3.3), all with _sliding_fused_kernel at 100%, so removing a dependent page-index->KV gather round trip (roughly 1 us of HBM latency with a cold L2) is the right kind of lever. Register and shared-memory cost is small: M=16, D=64, a 128x64 FP8 tile becomes 64 bf16 regs/thread for K and for V at 4 warps, with about 32 KB staged at 2 stages. The expected directions agree with the weights: sliding decode_1, 16 and 32 each carry weight 46, and verify and full shapes do not touch this kernel (sliding verify goes through FA3 on master, so the 'verify keeps BLOCK_N 64' clause is moot but harmless). Weakest link: with num_stages=2, Triton's software pipeliner may already issue iteration 2's page-index and K/V loads during iteration 1's dot and softmax, so the 'two dependent round trips' may really be closer to 1.3 round trips, and the saving could be well under 0.5 us, inside the 2-3.5% drift the md itself reports for sliding decode_1. Secondary risk: at decode_32 the grid is 1024 programs (several waves on 132 SMs), so a fatter tile per program that lowers occupancy could make that shape flat or slightly slower. That runs against the 'faster' expectation, but the per-shape rows make it readable either way. Prior: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-splits-32 (also one tile per program at batch 1, reached by doubling S) was neutral, though that change also doubled the combine width, so it does not refute this one.
confounders: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv: set S=16 at every decode batch, which is exactly what makes the chunk 128 keys = 2 tiles of 64; the hypothesis is a tuning of that landed config, not an independent change. With S tuned differently (8 -> 256 keys/program, 32 -> 64) BLOCK_N=128 would mean 2 tiles or a half-empty tile. That is a stacking dependency, not a confound: the measured delta is attributable to BLOCK_N at S=16.

sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: introduced _sliding_fused_kernel (num_warps=4, num_stages=2); the pipelining depth inherited from it decides how much of the second iteration's latency is already hidden, so the gain is conditional on that setting, but it is held fixed here.
fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads / full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv / FA3 pairing: not on the sliding decode path; no interaction expected beyond run-to-run drift on full shapes.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is a single constexpr on one kernel that owns 100% of the three target shapes' time, so the _sliding_fused_kernel profile rows on sliding decode_1/16/32 attribute any gain or loss directly. A revert of sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv would not isolate anything (it changes the tile count the hypothesis is premised on), and an ab-tune of num_stages (1 vs 2 at BLOCK_N=128) would only explain a null result, not disambiguate a gain or loss. If the result is null, the natural follow-up is a stacked num_stages/num_warps sweep, not a companion now. Judge on the kernel rows, as the md says, because sliding decode_1 headline drift (2-3.5%) is comparable to the expected effect.
open_questions: Does the compiled kernel at BLOCK_N=64, num_stages=2 actually pipeline the indirect (page-table -> K/V) loads across the 2-trip dynamic loop? If yes, the expected saving shrinks toward noise; a look at the TTGIR/PTX for cp.async or prefetch of iteration 2 would settle it before or after the run.
Should num_warps go to 8 together with BLOCK_N=128 (the 128x64 bf16 conversion of K and V doubles per-thread work)? Kept out by design; a candidate follow-up if decode_32 regresses.

If sliding-cuda-cluster-dsmem-onelaunch (running) lands and replaces this kernel on all sliding tp8/page-1 shapes, this result becomes moot; the scheduler should check that outcome before spending the run, or accept it as a cheap tuning of the fallback.
